title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
description: Users often complain that AI assistants such as ChatGPT are getting worse. Some versions do change, but human evaluation leaves a second possibility untested: the people judging may change. We separate the two on Chatbot Arena, a public platform where people compare answers from two anonymous large language models (LLMs) and pick the better one or say both are bad. We study 1,260,967 blind votes cast from May 2023 to August 2024 on pairs of models whose versions are fixed: dated vendor snapshots and models with fixed open weights. For the same pair of unchanged models, the share of votes saying "both are bad" rises by 1.71 percentage points a month on a mean of 17.1%, and by 1.91 points a month in 2024. In fourteen pairs observed often in both 2023 and 2024, it rose in every one, from 15.5% to 23.3%. The ranking does not trend: in 2024, the stronger model's share of decisive votes is flat. The rise holds within the same voter and on the same pair, and across arrival cohorts from their first recorded vote. It holds with prompt controls, in every major language, for dated vendor snapshots, open-weight models and models with stable answer length, and between interface changes. The drift is shared across models: month effects estimated from other models' pairs remove it from each model's own pairs. title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
description: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
description: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. title: Earlybird: Predictive Streaming Speech Recognition in 29M Parameters
description: Streaming speech recognizers output a word only after the speaker has finished it, typically 90-400 ms later. For a voice agent every millisecond counts: the sooner the words are outputted, the sooner the agent can start a search or plan its reply. We present Earlybird, a 29M-parameter streaming recognizer (16.8 MB at 4 bits). Earlybird learns from audio cut off at random points, including partway through a word, and is asked to predict every word that is due by then in full, plus a guess of the next two words. Its raw token probabilities give a confidence for every word including the one still being spoken. On clean audiobook speech (LibriSpeech test-clean), the median word is predicted correctly 90 ms before the speaker finishes it, while released streaming models get it 90 to 400 ms after it ends. Earlybird is the earliest on all six test sets we time, covering audiobooks, TED talks, public speech, earnings calls, and synthetic speech. On the same audiobooks, 69% of words are predicted correctly before they end, against 3-25% for the other models. For words still being spoken, confidence is calibrated, with an expected calibration error (ECE) of 3.7 to 5.5. On the eight English Open ASR Leaderboard sets, it is more accurate than Moonshine Tiny on every set and roughly ties Whistle, a model of the same size.
author: Sahil Mahendrakar

title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
description: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by having a draft model propose multiple tokens for the target model to verify in one pass. The speedup is governed by the expected acceptance length (EAL), yet standard training objectives such as cross-entropy, KL divergence, and total variation focus only on distribution matching or single-step overlap. Recent studies instead propose block-level training objectives, aiming to optimize EAL directly. However, these objectives remain surrogates rather than exact formulations of EAL. For example, some average later acceptance over target-distributed continuations rather than the verification branches selected by accepted tokens, introducing a covariance gap that can reverse the gradient direction. We analyze this gap and derive REAL, a real EAL training loss that uses path weights for unbiased estimation and Rao-Blackwellization for variance reduction. In a controlled loss-level comparison with a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B target and a Domino drafter, REAL outperforms WTV, VSD, DBLast, and the static LK baseline on probabilistic serving acceptance length across 9 task subsets and 5 evaluation seeds. These gains require only a change to the training loss, with no modification to the drafter architecture or inference procedure, demonstrating the practicality of real EAL training. A reference implementation of the REAL loss is available at https://github.com/King-ty/speculators/tree/real-loss.
author: Yu Tian

description: Research agents achieve increasingly strong benchmark scores, yet these scores do not necessarily translate into reliable delivery in ongoing research projects. Many research-agent benchmarks emphasize standalone tasks and relatively self-contained workflows in clean or curated workspaces. We introduce ARE-bench to evaluate whether research agents advance ongoing projects while respecting prior decisions and existing workspace state, grounded in real session context and in-progress workspaces. Each task is anchored at a real user request, preserves its requirements, and summarizes the earlier requests still in effect as background. The complete workspace is replayed to that boundary without cleanup, preserving artifacts from earlier turns. Each checklist is compiled from an intent-aligned rubric and credits any valid solution. title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
description: Rapidly evolving LLM architectures and heterogeneous mobile hardware make supporting new models in on-device inference engines a recurring and costly system challenge. Each model may require coordinated changes across conversion, graph construction, operators, and hardware backends. Existing coding agents often miss these cross-layer dependencies and struggle to diagnose failures across host--device execution paths. We present EngineAgent, an agentic system for automating on-device LLM model enablement. Its key insight is to separate reusable engine and hardware knowledge from model-specific implementation. Before enablement, EngineAgent constructs a hierarchy-aware engine index that captures engine abstraction layers and cross-layer dependencies, and pre-validates backend-specific build, execution, and debugging workflows using already supported models. For each new model, a builder uses this knowledge to coordinate cross-layer changes, while an auditor checks implementation completeness and drives iterative debugging through device-side validation. Across 12 tasks spanning three mobile LLMs and four engine--backend pairs on CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, EngineAgent achieves 75% end-to-end success with either of two underlying LLMs, versus 33.3% for the strongest coding-agent baseline. Success requires compilation, on-device execution, and output-logit agreement with reference implementations. title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making

title: An AI Assistant for Automating Anti-Corruption Expertise of Draft Legislation Based on the TRACE Framework
description: We present an AI assistant for automating anti-corruption expertise of draft legislation based on the TRACE architecture, designed to screen bills for corruption risks: pinpoint provisions an expert would criticise and name the regulatory defect in each. The pipeline combines a deterministic parsing core, model-guided single-provision qualification, rule-based factor assignment, and external human oversight. To evaluate the assistant, we constructed an open benchmark from the published conclusions of Ukraine's National Agency on Corruption Prevention (NAZK), comprising 132 draft laws with 474 model-extracted findings. A system flag agrees with a finding when it targets a compatible provision and an LLM judge rates the risk as the same (strict) or partly the same (lenient). On 100 draft laws, the pipeline matches 0.28 of the findings within its top ten flags using the local Gemma 4 31B model, 0.30 with Sonnet 5.5, and 0.43-0.46 across all flags (non-blind; the frozen blind baseline achieves 0.21, 95% CI 0.16-0.26). Across all runs, most misses occur on provisions that the system located but qualified as a different risk, and none of the 32 legal-collision findings was matched. On 21 acts held out from tuning, the pipeline outperforms a monolithic prompt containing the full methodology under the strict measure, though not under the lenient one, and Opus 5.5 adds nothing over Sonnet. title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
description: Variability in syntactic structure and parsing ambiguity are fundamental aspects of natural language which modern LLMs have to learn to deal with proficiently. Previous "post-mortem" studies have shown that fully trained Transformers indeed approximate canonical parsing algorithms such as inside-outside, but little is established theoretically about how this is actually learned. Here, we make a first step towards addressing this by studying the learning dynamics in synthetic context-free grammars with variable parse tree topology. The stagewise learning curves are fully interpretable, in the sense that all of the loss stages a) can be computed analytically, and b) can be clearly associated to the representation of a hidden latent tree variable, which allows to lift ambiguity and utilize information from wider contexts. By probing representations, we visualize the emergence of inside-outside computation across depth and during training: while during early stages local (bigram/trigram) information is used and involves only a few initial layers, gradually the Transformer develops an encoder-decoder structure where the most abstract latent information is encoded in the middle, and the latter half of the network is used to progressively refine the final token prediction. title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
description: During extended wakefulness, mammalian neocortical networks experience localized periods of transient neuronal silence termed off-states. Here, we examine how analogous spatiotemporally concentrated disruptions affect sequential reasoning in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). Evaluating 250 paired derivations on the GSM8K benchmark across two 8B models (Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct), we contrast clustered bursts of attention head masking against budget-matched diffuse i.i.d. dropout. Concentrated bursts induce substantial reasoning degradation: at onset parameter $\mathcal{B}=0.10$ (scheduling $\sim 5.7\%$ of vulnerable head-token volume), Qwen3-8B accuracy drops from $91.2\%$ under diffuse noise to $78.8\%$ under burst dropout ($Δ= -12.4$ percentage points [pp], exact McNemar $p = 5.5 \times 10^{-6}$), while LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct drops from $84.0\%$ to $76.8\%$ ($Δ= -7.2$ pp, $p = 0.0198$). Conversely, dispersing the identical cumulative budget uniformly across generation steps via stratified quintile matching yields substantially milder degradation (retaining $91.2\%$ in Qwen and $84.0\%$ in LLaMA). In an exploratory factorial dissociation ($N=100$), single-step dropout density is associated with an acute drop in a single schedule draw ($-10.0$ pp on Qwen, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.0425$), while multi-token continuity exhibits an inconclusive compounding trend ($-7.0$ pp, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.1892$). title: HandsOnAid: Building and Evaluating an Offline First-Aid Assistant for Emergency Response Scenarios
description: Emergencies can occur where there is no phone signal and no ambulance nearby. A small language model on a phone can be helpful in such situations, but its advice needs to be safe and accurate. We built HandsOnAid, a 4-bit Gemma 2B model fine-tuned with QLoRA on FirstAidQA dataset, a corpus of 5,550 first-aid question-answer pairs. We compared seven configurations, including the base, 4-bit and 8-bit fine-tuned models, and versions with a length floor, safety gate, or retrieval. We used a 41-pair question-answer bank with medically reviewed references that followed ANZCOR guidelines, and a strict 0-5 score rubric, with twelve safety overrides. Four frontier LLM judges (GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM-5.3) blindly scored every answer, with 45 hidden controls used to check judge reliability. Fine-tuning improved the mean score by +1.08 over the base model to 2.34. The best configuration scored 2.51 out of 5 which was the fine-tuned 4-bit model with retrieval. A medical professional also conducted a blind evaluation of 40 answers across the base, the 4-bit fine-tuned, and the retrieval configurations, and the scores were similar to the LLM judges' average scores. A keyword audit found limited coverage of several details of ANZCOR guidelines in the training corpus, that are required by the rubric, which suggests that missing information in the training data could be a cause of the low scores. title: Lily (Wuthering Waves) / 莉莉（鸣潮） [LORA/Anima]
description:
中文说明

《鸣潮》Lily 的角色 LoRA，底模 Anima。

素材来自游戏内照相模式：一百一十一张 4K 原片，覆盖全身、半身、脸、背面、服装细节，全部无 UI。这批素材的一致性比搜图拼出来的高一档。

画风说明：素材是 3D 渲染，但训出来的图是二维动漫风，没带塑料感——模型只学了人和衣服，没把渲染质感带进去。

已知短板：眼睛颜色要手动压（见上，训练词里写错了）；头发容易被画成侧辫而不是披散。

触发词与特征串

lili, 1girl, solo, long hair, purple hair, light purple hair,
black dress, white lace, frilled dress, black veil,
white thighhighs, black shoes

眼睛必须写对。 她是紫瞳，瞳孔里有十字形高光。训练词里我错写成 blue eyes，所以出图时要靠提示词压：

  • 正面 (purple eyes:1.5), (pink purple eyes:1.3), (cross-shaped pupils:1.2)

  • 负面 (blue eyes:1.4)

头饰是一圈小花，不是单朵：

(ring of small white flowers:1.4), (flower crown:1.2)

推荐参数

  • LoRA 权重：0.85

  • steps 32 / cfg 4

  • 底模：anima-base-v1.0 效果最好，reed 系也能用

title: The Fur Wardrobe [LORA/Krea 2]
description:
So, I says to myself, I says… Why toss coats into blender? Why not try making a LoRA based on one coat?

But the training data, you say, too thin, too homogeneous! Yes, solid points, but I flaunt my vibe-coded variety generator app, API key, and frontier image models at you. And the ten bucks I threw at them… Don’t mention Qwen, it’s… not great at inferring what fur looks like from different angles, and I’ll leave it at that.

This page will be updated with new coats as… I feel like it.

One important general note about all of them: they will be ‘less flexible’ than the generalist LoRAs. By that I mean they will try to create the exact coat they are trained on. If there’s something about the coat you don’t like, I’d skip that one. On all other things, they should be flexible: lighting and character for example.

Coat 2: Jacket-length blue fox.

Because sometimes less is more. Besi

title: Shit's On Fire, Yo (IL/PD/XL) [LORA/Illustrious]
description:
The pose from the semi-famous Rennaissance painting Portrait of a Young Man (1561) by Allessandro Allori (1535 – 1607). Because sometimes you just gotta point out that shit's on fire, yo.

Not to be confused with a certain "1980s yuppie in a raincoat pointing at a stereo system" meme. Because that one goes in the other direction. And is, of course, far less classy. Also not to be confused with "this is fine" - Shit being On Fire, Yo, is not fine.

The dataset for this is hilariously cludged together, but it seems to work well enough for the pose at least. You may have to inpaint or just paste in the shit being on fire, yo, at least if it's supposed to be something very specific. The trigger's just "allori" but I suggest adding "pointing, looking at viewer, facing viewer", etc to finetune it.

title: rococo penthouse [LORA/SDXL 1.0]
description:
ENGLISH

I created r0c0c0 p3nth0us3 around a simple idea: what if rococo luxury owned the horizon? This photorealistic background dataset explores a modern triplex penthouse at the top of a skyscraper. Ivory lacquer, champagne gold, pale blush, marble, crystal and translucent silk connect eleven distinct spaces. A small golden rocaille shell paperweight appears throughout as a discreet signature.

Inside the set: a grand panoramic salon, glass-domed reception rotunda, infinity pool over the void, hanging garden terrace, minimalist night suite, private elevator hall, spa and hammam, champagne bar, cinema-boudoir, curved library gallery and private rooftop heliport. A final overhead atrium image brings the three levels together.

The 45 training images contain no people. I designed clear central areas for character placement, with peripheral furniture and several camera heights. Pool compositions use unobstructed water at the center. The suite keeps its bed to the side.

title: Ani3D 40 IL - Maximum Render Lift (Illustrious) [Checkpoint/Illustrious]
description:
Ani3D 40 is the practical ceiling (alpha = 0.40): the heaviest 3D-render treatment in the series with anime faces still readable.

[Recipe] Add-difference merge on UNet only: Nova Anime XL IL v19.0 + 0.40 x (Nova Orange XL REX v1.0 - Nova Reality XL IL v9.0). VAE and text encoders inherited from the base model; fp16 safetensors, no baked LoRA.

[Why this direction] Nova 3DCG minus Nova Reality isolates a 3D-render delta: volumetric lighting, glossier shading and cleaner speculars. Adding it to Nova Anime gives game-CG style rendering without abandoning anime faces or tag behaviour.

[Series] Ani3D IL is one base and one direction at four strengths: 10 / 20 / 30 / 40. 10 is a subtle render sheen, 20 is a clear 3D-anime look, 30 is game-CG territory, and 40 is the strongest render lift that still keeps anime faces intact.

[Recommended settings] Euler a, 24-28 steps, CFG 5.0-5.5, 832x1216. Hires fix above 1.25x helps skin and fabric; Dan

  • higher structural similarity

  • stronger saturation changes

title: velvet womb [LORA/Krea 2]
description:
ENGLISH

With v3lv3t w0mb, I wanted to create the decadent private suite of an imaginary organic civilization: velvet, dark nacre, gold veins and warm light, with glamour and unease sharing the same rooms. The sensuality comes from the decor and sculpted architecture. The spaces remain empty, still and ready to receive a character.

The dataset contains 45 square background images across eleven locations: the membrane-alcove bedroom, shadow-tendril salon, nacre springs bathroom, private liqueurs bar, valve-door corridor, retina-mirror dressing suite, private amber steam grotto, wardrobe lodge, night-garden balcony, nerve-like vertical elevator and monumental jaw-inspired reception hall. A final master-chamber view brings the suite together. A champagne flute on a side table serves as a recurring visual detail; its appearance varies between views.

Trigger: v3lv3t w0mb

Suggested starting strength: 0.8-1.0, as an untested starting point to adjust after training. T
